learning_outcomes.text: Student knows and understands the basics of statics.
Student knows and understands the basics of material strength; simple and complex strength, permissible stresses, fatigue strength.
Student knows and understands the principles of constructing mechanical systems using separable and non-separable joints and rotary motion assemblies.
Student can solve problems in statics and determine reactions for bending and torsion beams.
Student can solve problems related to simple, complex, and fatigue strength.
Student can design mechanical systems based on separable and non-separable joints and rotary motion assemblies.
Student can operate in the area of creating technical documentation for design tasks.
Student can cooperate in a project team.

syllabus_topics: Auditorium classes (all classes 2 hours each): 1. Introduction. Regulations, grading method and credit for exercises (three tests and two design tasks; grades from consultations and final project grade). Division into design teams, consultation dates. Literature. Brief discussion of the topic: "Types and reactions of constraints (supports)".
2. Basics of statics. Solving statics problems (by students for previously assigned topics): a) concurrent force system, b) parallel force system, c) determining reactions for bending beams.
3. Basics of statics. Solving statics problems: a) arbitrary force system, b) determining centers of gravity for (lines, flat surfaces, and solids).
4. Basics of statics. Test I (test covers 3 problems from basics of statics).
5. Basics of material strength. Solving problems of simple strength – tension of rods (statically determinate systems and statically indeterminate systems).
6. Basics of material strength. Solving problems of simple strength – torsion of circular symmetry rods and bending of beams with arbitrary cross-section.
7. Basics of material strength. Test II (test covers 3 problems from basics of material strength). Assistant: discussion of design task I, data for the project.
8. Basics of separable joint design. Solving problems of bolted joints (depending on the loading method and application of bolted joints in flexible systems).
9. Basics of separable joint design. Solving problems of bolted joints; cont. and pin and key joints. 1st consultation for design task I.
10. Basics of non-separable joint design. Solving problems of welded joints (using butt and fillet welds under simple and complex loads). 2nd consultation for design task I.

11. Basics of separable and non-separable joint design. Test III (test covers 3 problems from basics of separable and non-separable joint design). Collection and credit for design task I. Assistant: discussion of design task II, data for the project.
12. Basics of rotary motion assembly design. 1st consultation for design task II.
13. Basics of rotary motion assembly design. Collection and credit for design task II.
14. Credit. Credit for design tasks and tests. Credit for exercises.
Lectures: 1. Basics of statics; concurrent, parallel and arbitrary force systems. Determining reactions for bending and torsion beams. Determining centers of gravity (5h).
2. Basics of material strength; simple strength – tension and compression, shear, torsion, bending. Permissible stresses. Statically indeterminate systems (6h).
3. Complex strength – theories of effort. Fatigue strength; determining the safety factor under variable loads (2h).
4. Basics of separable joint design; calculations and selection of bolted, shaped (pin, key, spline) joints. Principles of selection and designation of construction materials (6h).
5. Basics of non-separable joint design; calculations and design of welded, brazed and glued joints (4h).
6. Basics of design of rotary motion elements and assemblies (shafts, belt drives, rolling bearings) (5h).
assessment_rules: The method of verification of learning outcomes for lectures and auditorium classes includes activity during classes, tests, engineering projects, and oral answers. The credit for auditorium classes is based on oral or written statements in the form of colloquia, which contribute to the final grade for this form of classes.
